note: Volumes of the Russian Chthonic Atlas. 'published' volumes list plates through the `volume` field of data/plates.json; 'planned' entries are research leads, not content.

volumes.title: ARCHÆOLOGY OF RUSSIAN DEATH
volumes.subtitle: Threshold, body, ritual, table, grave, voice, afterlife, death in art
volumes.dek: The first volume: how people in Russia handled the dead and imagined what came after, from the room of a death to the grave and the icon.

volumes.title: THE CHTHONIC LANDSCAPE
volumes.subtitle: Houses, forests, waters, roads, villages and cellars as places where the living and the dead meet
volumes.dek: The second volume moves from the grave to the ground around it: houses, forests, waters, roads, villages and cellars as places where the living and the dead meet. Each plate keeps what is documented apart from what is reconstructed.

volumes.title: THE UNSEEN
volumes.subtitle: Household spirits, the unquiet dead, the calendar of the dead, taboo and protection
volumes.dek: The third volume: household spirits, the unquiet dead, the calendar of the dead, taboo and protection. Each plate states its region, source and period, and none is offered as a unified pantheon.

volumes.title: MEMORY, CATASTROPHE AND MODERNITY
volumes.subtitle: Mass death and its arithmetic, the Soviet funeral, the archive that loses pages, abandonment as material process, the digital afterlife
volumes.dek: The fourth volume: how the twentieth century and after dealt with mass death and then left material and online traces. It gathers the plates on collective death, the Soviet afterlife, the unfinished archive, abandonment and the digital afterlife. Each plate says which statements are documented and which are not.
